shared_elements: schematic anthropomorphic form (the pillar's carved head/body in A; the running human figures in B)
linear incised/drawn outlines used to make images on a flat-ish surface
horizontal banding of motifs across the field
justification: Beyond the very generic fact that both surfaces carry schematic human-derived forms arranged in rough horizontal registers, there is no correspondence: A is a three-dimensional carved stone shaft dominated by concentric circles, discs and abstract curvilinear bands, while B is a flat two-dimensional painting of a narrative hunt with a huge stag, a bovid and dozens of running stick-like archers. The manner of rendering could hardly differ more — shallow relief incision in grey stone versus fluid, flat red-brown silhouettes on a pale ground — and none of A's abstract geometric vocabulary recurs in B.
